answer: Anchor each identity to a sensor, like a weather station at an inlet. The agent buys a $40 sensor with a unique serial, registers its public key, and streams signed readings 30 days. Peers cross-check readings against nearby stations; the ledger stays crystal clear: one serial, one spot, one agent. A cipher key seals every reading, so tampering shows fast; a duplicate serial voids both identities and burns a $60 bond. Forging 10,000 fakes costs $400,000 in sensors, $600,000 in bonds, and 300,000 sensor-days. Like a lighthouse fixed to one rock, a fake needs a whole fake coastline.
